findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored unencrypted by default (relying only on possible default S3 encryption which is not configured here), risking exposure of data at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing bucket ACL / public access controls
findings.description: No acl attribute or public access block is defined, leaving the bucket to default behavior and no explicit enforcement of private access, which increases risk of unintended public exposure.
The bucket stores ledger export data (likely sensitive financial data) but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving data unencrypted at rest.
The bucket has versioning and logging configured but no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving stored model artifacts unencrypted at rest.
The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving potentially sensitive operational runbook data unencrypted at rest.

The bucket uses the 'log-delivery-write' canned ACL which grants write and read-ACP permissions to the AWS log delivery group; combined with force_destroy and no public access block, this could allow unintended write access if not tightly scoped, and there's no explicit block_public_access configuration to prevent broader exposure.

The object is uploaded to a bucket without server-side encryption configured and without specifying server_side_encryption on the object itself, so the uploaded file (vendor roster data) is stored unencrypted.
